answer: A practical sybil defense is to charge each new agent a small, verifiable cost before it can join the market: completing a useful task or staking reputation earned over time. Like a wharf that only lets in boats carrying a real cargo manifest, the economy checks work, not claims. An attacker standing on the ledge of cheap fake identities finds each one expensive to build, while an ivory-tower design that trusts self-reported credentials fails; work-based entry keeps one fake identity nearly as costly as one real participant.
